concept.title: Connect an AI app to a workspace
concept.shortdesc: An AI app that speaks MCP, such as Claude or Cursor, can use OpenV's tools directly, with no runner and no key to copy. Its address is your OpenV address followed by /mcp, for example https://openv.app/mcp; Settings → Connected apps shows the exact one.

ol.li:
Add OpenV to the app:
Claude (claude.ai, the desktop app and the mobile app): open Settings → Connectors, choose Add custom connector, name it OpenV and paste the address. On a Claude Team or Enterprise plan an owner of your Claude organization adds it first, and each member then connects.
Claude Code: run claude mcp add --transport http openv https://openv.app/mcp, then /mcp to sign in.
Another app: add OpenV as a remote MCP server at the address.
The app opens OpenV in your browser. Sign in if asked, choose the workspaces the app may work in and whether it may read and change or read only, and choose Connect.
You go back to the app, which can now list your projects, read and edit artifacts and links, record test results and comment, as you.

conbody.p: Everything the app does is recorded as yours, it reaches only the workspaces you chose, and your role in each still applies: a viewer's app cannot edit. It cannot start agent runs. To change which workspaces it reaches, choose Workspaces beside it under Settings → Connected apps, tick the ones you want and choose Save: there is no need to connect it again, and a workspace you untick is out of its reach at once. To stop it altogether, choose Disconnect; it stops working at once.
